dossier.public_summary: The light-curve shows two deep dips that alternate with shallow or absent dips, a classic sign of a stellar eclipse at twice the reported period. Depths also change enormously between sectors and transits, so the 11.5-day signal cannot be a stable planet transit.

reasons.why: Strong odd-even depth difference with 9.0-sigma 6524 ppm even transit and near-zero odd transit points to a binary at twice the 11.5 d period, not a planet.

Depths are wildly inconsistent and dominated by two deep events; depth_change_pct 161 and sectors.p_constant 1.9e-22 with sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source show real variability beyond aperture differences.

reasons.why: Even within the QLP source depth changes by >4x, confirming the signal is not a stable planet on the calibrated target but a few deep dips folded inconsistently.
